svg.title: HyperWeave
svg.desc: HyperWeave glyph: cushion in ionized pearl-chrome with a hairline chrome rim, true negative-space gem window, breathing core.

hw:reasoning.hw:intent: The glyph as pearl chrome, nothing more: hero DNA carried by the material of the cushion itself, with the gem window returned to a true hole.
hw:reasoning.hw:approach: Two defects fixed from v0.3.0. FILLED WINDOW: baking a pool inside the gem violated the negative-space doctrine — the hero window shows the pool because the pool is behind the whole banner, not inside the mark; the standalone glyph now cuts the window as a true evenodd hole again and carries the hero DNA as material: the ionized pearl-chrome ramp on the cushion body. CUTOFF TIPS: the ramp's pure #FFFFFF bookends made the diamond tips vanish on white surfaces, reading as clipped; bookends softened to #F2FAFF / #E6F4FE and a 0.6px chrome rim (#7AB8E8) traces the full evenodd outline — outer diamond and window — so the silhouette is closed on any surface.
hw:reasoning.hw:tradeoffs: Back to composite-only: dropping the baked pool loses the living water at icon scale, traded for the doctrine (the window composits whatever surface sits behind it) and for 16px survival. The rim is the one addition the 0.1.0 spec did not have — accepted because a chrome object needs an edge the instant its highlights match the page.
hw:reasoning.hw:spatial-notes: 64x64, bilateral about (32,32); cushion cardinals +/-29; gem window ~32.6x43.5 girdle, true hole; ramp y 3-61 with near-white bookends; rim 0.6px on the full evenodd path; core r2 breathing to 2.6 with r3.2 halo at 0.15.
